Below is a quick‑look list of the **federal public holidays that create a 3‑day weekend** in Canada for the year 2023.  
(If a holiday falls on a weekend, the following Monday is usually observed, giving you a “long weekend.”)  

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Day of Week | Notes |
|-------------|---------|-------------|-------|
| **Jan 2** | New Year’s Day (observed) | Monday | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday, so it was observed on Monday. |
| **Feb 20** | Family Day (Ontario) | Monday | Third Monday in February. |
| **Apr 7** | Good Friday | Friday | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Fri‑Sat‑Sun). |
| **May 24** | Victoria Day | Monday | Celebrates Queen Victoria’s birthday; first Monday in May. |
| **Jul 3** | Canada Day (observed) | Monday | Canada Day fell on Saturday, so it was observed on Monday. |
| **Sep 4** | Labour Day | Monday | First Monday in September. |
| **Oct 9** | Thanksgiving | Monday | Second Monday in October. |
| **Nov 13** | Remembrance Day (observed) | Monday | Remembrance Day fell on Saturday, so it was observed on Monday. |
| **Dec 25** | Christmas Day | Monday | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Fri‑Sat‑Sun‑Mon). |

> **Pro‑Tip:**  
> • If you’re planning trips in a specific province, check for *provincial* holidays that also create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, St. Jean‑Baptiste Day in Québec, etc.).  
> • Some provinces observe holidays on the nearest weekday if they fall on a weekend, so the dates above are the *observed* dates that give you the extra day off.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app! If you need the provincial long weekends for a particular province, just let me know.
